business_problem: Cathay Property Insurance was adopting large models across outbound calling, customer service, and content generation, but every provider had different request formats, authentication methods, and cost visibility. The company needed one way to govern multi-model access, tenant permissions, content safety, audit trails, and token-based spend across both internal and external model providers.
solution_summary: Cathay Property Insurance standardized its growing LLM estate behind Alibaba Cloud's cloud-native API Gateway so model consumption could be governed as infrastructure rather than as one-off integrations. The gateway gives the insurer a unified protocol surface across more than a dozen model providers and hides each vendor's distinct request and response structure from downstream business teams. It also centralizes API key custody, multi-tenant authentication, and consumer-level access control so different internal or external callers can use approved models without directly handling model-provider credentials. Around that access layer, Cathay connected Alibaba Cloud Content Security for request and response inspection, and enabled AI observability across metrics, logs, and traces so token usage can be attributed by request, model, and consumer. The result is a governed model-access plane that supports customer-service and content workflows while lowering compliance and cost-management risk.

solution_components.name: Cloud-native API Gateway
solution_components.role: Provides the unified access layer for multiple model providers, authentication, routing, and token observability.

solution_components.name: Content Security
solution_components.role: Scans inbound and outbound model content for sensitive or unsafe text before it is accepted.

solution_components.name: Higress
solution_components.role: Supplies the Envoy-based gateway core for hot updates, stream handling, and protection against AI-specific traffic attacks.

data_flow: Business applications send LLM requests through Cloud-native API Gateway, which normalizes provider protocols, applies authentication and tenant policy, and forwards traffic to the selected model provider. Request and response payloads are scanned by Content Security, while metrics, logs, traces, and token counts are recorded so Cathay can audit usage and control cost after responses are returned.
business_outcome: Cathay moved all large-model traffic behind a single governance layer and made sensitive-content inspection, consumer attribution, and cost observation mandatory rather than optional. The company can now scale model-backed insurance workflows while knowing who used each token, which scenario used it, and whether risky content or abnormal consumption needs intervention.
metrics: supports nearly 100 million tokens of model traffic per day
all model traffic now proxies through the cloud-native API gateway
architecture_clues: The insurer uses one gateway abstraction to normalize heterogeneous model-provider protocols before business apps consume them.
Token observability is a first-class control and is recorded by request, model, and consumer rather than only at the aggregate level.
The gateway is also part of the safety posture, with content scanning and traceable audit hooks for risky conversations.
